name: Purple Team, BAS & Adversary Emulation
tagline: Validate your detections by emulating real adversaries, running atomic TTPs, and mapping coverage against MITRE ATT&CK.

tools.name: MITRE Caldera
tools.desc: Automated adversary emulation platform (now an Apache project) built on ATT&CK: deploy agents, craft adversary profiles from techniques, and run them against your estate.
tools.when: Build a repeatable adversary operation once and re-run it after every detection change or control rollout.

tools.name: Adversary Emulation Library
tools.desc: MITRE Center for Threat-Informed Defense's full (APT29, FIN6, Turla) and micro (webshells, process injection) emulation plans in human-readable plus machine-readable YAML for Caldera.
tools.when: Execute a threat-intel-grounded scenario as a ready-made purple-team script instead of writing one from scratch.

tools.name: PurpleSharp
tools.desc: C# adversary simulation tool that executes ATT&CK-mapped TTPs purely from Windows endpoints (process execution, scheduled tasks, WMI, Kerberos abuse) without needing a C2.
tools.when: Run in-host purple exercises fast: trigger technique sequences and immediately check which SIEM/EDR detections fired.

tools.name: Atomic Red Team
tools.desc: MITRE-aligned library of small, portable detection tests; each atomic test documents a technique's exact procedure plus the logs and telemetry a defender should see if the detection works.
tools.when: Prove a specific detection fires by running the precise TTP procedure it was built to catch.

tools.name: AtomicTestHarnesses
tools.desc: Red Canary's PowerShell module (Python for macOS/Linux) that executes many variations of a single technique and validates the telemetry each variation generates.
tools.when: Check your detections hold up across technique variants, not just the single canonical procedure.

tools.name: Stratus Red Team
tools.desc: Datadog's granular cloud emulation library — 'Atomic Red Team for the cloud' — detonating AWS, Azure, GCP, Entra ID, and K8s techniques mapped to ATT&CK with automatic warmup and cleanup.
tools.when: Validate cloud SIEM detections against real TTPs in a dedicated sandbox cloud account, never production.

tools.name: CloudGoat 2
tools.desc: Rhino Security Labs' 'Vulnerable by Design' AWS/Azure deployment tool that builds intentionally vulnerable, CTF-style scenarios for practicing cloud attack paths.
tools.when: Stand up an authorized practice range in a throwaway cloud account to rehearse TTPs before running real emulation.

tools.name: MITRE ATT&CK Navigator
tools.desc: Web app for annotating and exploring ATT&CK matrices via shareable layer files; load emulation-plan technique lists to plan what you are about to run.
tools.when: Scope an emulation exercise by marking the techniques on the matrix before touching any platform.

tools.name: MITRE ATT&CK
tools.desc: The authoritative knowledge base: adversary tactics, techniques, sub-techniques, threat groups, and the data sources needed to detect them.
tools.when: Resolve technique IDs and read detection guidance before any scoring, emulation, or rule building.

tools.name: rogueai
tools.desc: Agentic AI red-team — autonomous decide->execute->observe->reflect loops against own-lab targets with human-in-the-loop safety gates.
tools.when: Automated adversarial emulation in a sandbox you control.

tools.name: Infection Monkey
tools.desc: Open-source BAS platform (Guardicore/Akamai) whose agent self-propagates across a network via real exploiters and misconfiguration checks, reporting findings to the Monkey Island console.
tools.when: Automated lateral-movement and control-gap testing on a lab segment or isolated data-center island.

tools.name: OpenBAS
tools.desc: Filigran's open-source breach-and-attack simulation platform (now evolving into OpenAEV) for planning, scheduling, and running adversary-simulation campaigns and crisis exercises.
tools.when: When you need a free multi-team BAS platform that couples technical simulations with exercise tracking, integrated with OpenCTI threat intel.

tools.name: SafeBreach Validate
tools.desc: Commercial BAS pioneer: lightweight simulators on endpoints, network, and cloud run 30,000+ attack methods from its Hacker's Playbook to continuously validate controls.
tools.when: Continuous, enterprise-scale security-control validation when you have budget for a licensed BAS product.

tools.name: AttackIQ
tools.desc: MITRE ATT&CK-aligned BAS platform with a free AttackIQ Flex tier and a large scenario library that continuously exercises prevention, detection, and response controls.
tools.when: Continuous control validation with ATT&CK coverage reporting baked into the vendor platform.

tools.name: Cymulate
tools.desc: BAS platform that deploys lightweight agents to simulate the full kill chain plus exposure management, scoring security posture with prioritized remediation guidance.
tools.when: Benchmark your controls against sector peers and get prioritized gap remediation from one dashboard.

tools.name: DetectionLab
tools.desc: Chris Long's Packer/Vagrant suite that builds a Windows domain pre-loaded with Sysmon, WEF, osquery, and Splunk plus hardened logging defaults (no longer actively maintained since 2023, but still widely used).
tools.when: Spin up a known-good instrumented AD lab to test detections against realistic Windows telemetry.

tools.name: DetectionLab Primer
tools.desc: The official DetectionLab documentation/introduction: architecture, deployment guides for VirtualBox, AWS, Azure, and Hyper-V, and walkthroughs of each pre-installed tool.
tools.when: Read before first build so you pick the right provider and understand what logging you are getting.

tools.name: Splunk Attack Range
tools.desc: Splunk Threat Research Team's Terraform/Ansible range that deploys instrumented AWS/Azure/GCP labs, runs Atomic Red Team and PurpleSharp simulations, and forwards telemetry into Splunk.
tools.when: Develop and CI-test Splunk detections against reproducible attack data in an isolated cloud range.

tools.name: Purple Team Exercise Framework (PTEF)
tools.desc: SCYTHE's industry-standard methodology (v4) for designing purple-team exercises: planning templates, TTP mapping spreadsheets, emulation-plan formats, and a maturity model.
tools.when: Structure your first (or fiftieth) purple exercise so CTI, red, and blue roles, evidence collection, and lessons-learned are all defined up front.

tools.name: OWASP PurpleTeam
tools.desc: OWASP's open purpleteam tooling: an orchestrator with TLS and application scanning components that run coordinated security tests and report results for CI use.
tools.when: Add repeatable purpleteam-style scanning checks to an application/TLS hardening pipeline.

tools.name: DeTT&CT
tools.desc: Rabobank's framework to administer and score data-source quality, visibility, and detection per ATT&CK technique, then export the resulting coverage as ATT&CK Navigator layers.
tools.when: Build a scored, evidence-based map of detection and visibility coverage and prioritize blue-team effort on the gaps.

tools.name: MITRE ATT&CK Navigator
tools.desc: Web app for annotating and exploring ATT&CK matrices via shareable layer files; load DeTT&CT or VECTR output to render coverage heatmaps.
tools.when: Visualize and communicate detection coverage across the matrix during and after purple exercises.

tools.name: MITRE CAR
tools.desc: MITRE Cyber Analytics Repository: a curated set of analytics, each tied to ATT&CK techniques with data requirements, pseudocode, and reference implementations for validating detections.
tools.when: Find analytics worth implementing when you know which ATT&CK technique you need coverage for.

tools.name: MITRE D3FEND
tools.desc: Counter-adversary engineering knowledge graph of digital artifacts, tactics, and hardening techniques — the defensive counterpart to ATT&CK for describing how countermeasures work.
tools.when: Name and structure defensive countermeasures precisely when documenting what each control actually prevents.

tools.name: MITRE SHIELD
tools.desc: Active defense knowledge base of techniques defenders can use to engage adversaries (deception, hunting, hardening), mapped to ATT&CK for planning proactive defense operations.
tools.when: Plan proactive or deception-based defenses that complement your detection coverage map.

tools.name: yara-x
tools.desc: VirusTotal's Rust rewrite of YARA with a strict compiler that surfaces syntax errors and warnings early, plus a fast CLI for scanning samples with your rules.
tools.when: Compile and regression-test YARA rules in CI — stricter diagnostics catch broken rules before deployment.

tools.name: YARA
tools.desc: The de-facto pattern-matching engine for malware rules; `yara -w` compiles rule sets and flags syntax problems before you scan anything.
tools.when: The baseline check: compile your rules locally and run them against known samples to confirm hits and false positives.

tools.name: CIRCL yara-validator
tools.desc: CIRCL's Python validator that compiles batches of YARA rules, reports which are broken, and attempts automatic repairs on include-related breakage.
tools.when: Bulk-validate a shared rule repository before merging changes.

tools.name: YaraValidator online
tools.desc: Free web validator that compiles rules against current YARA and YARA-X versions to catch compatibility issues without any local install.
tools.when: Instant one-off compatibility check of a rule paste across engine versions.

tools.name: Sigma
tools.desc: Vendor-agnostic detection rule format with a converter ecosystem that turns portable Sigma rules into Splunk, Elastic, QRadar, Sentinel, and dozens of other query languages.
tools.when: Write detection content once and compile it to every SIEM you run; the shared syntax is also easy to unit-test.

tools.name: Sigma CLI
tools.desc: Official SigmaHQ CLI (sigma-cli) that converts, validates, and tests Sigma rules against backend plugins, catching broken syntax and unsupported constructs.
tools.when: Automate rule conversion and linting in CI so bad Sigma never reaches a SIEM.

tools.name: Elastic detection-rules
tools.desc: Elastic's production rule repository with prebuilt and custom Sigma-style rules, plus tooling (detection-rules CLI) to unit-test, version, and package rules for the Elastic Stack.
tools.when: Benchmark your own rule quality against vendor-maintained content and test rules before shipping to Elastic.

tools.name: VECTR
tools.desc: Free purple-team platform (Security Risk Advisors) that tracks red/blue test cases, campaigns, and per-tool detection/prevention outcomes measured against MITRE ATT&CK over time.
tools.when: Record exercise results and trend detection coverage over months so purple-team improvements are measurable.

tools.name: MITRE Attack Flow
tools.desc: Center for Threat-Informed Defense's STIX-based format and tooling for modeling how adversary behaviors chain together within an operation or campaign.
tools.when: Document the full flow of an emulated campaign — not just isolated techniques — for reporting and ATT&CK mapping.
